title: Unit tests for a quota-checked upload service
name: Upload quota tests

questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how these unit tests verify the UploadService's behavior? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
In the test "removes the stored blob when recording usage fails", what does the final assertion that blobs.objects.size is 0 actually show about UploadService?
choices: That the quota check rejected the upload before put was called
That put was never called because addUsage runs first
That the blob was written and then deleted in the catch block after addUsage threw
Nothing, because blobs was recreated for this test

questions.prompt: Why does the "accepts an upload that exactly fills the quota" test matter as a separate case?
choices: It checks that Promise.all reads usage and limit concurrently
It pins down the boundary of `data.byteLength > remaining`, catching a change to `>=`
It verifies that etags are derived from the byte length
It ensures the leading slash is stripped from the path

questions.prompt: Each test gets fresh InMemoryQuotas and InMemoryBlobs from beforeEach. What is the main benefit compared to constructing them once for the whole file?
choices: Tests run faster because fewer objects are allocated
It allows the tests to run in parallel worker threads sharing the maps
It is required for async tests to be awaited correctly
State set by one test, such as usage of 900, cannot leak into another and make results depend on test order
